what_it_does: FPGAs (Field-Programmable Gate Arrays) are chips where engineers can reprogram the logic gates after manufacturing. Today's FPGAs are 2D—wires and gates laid flat on silicon. FPGen-3D automates the design of 3D FPGAs, stacking logic vertically to use the chip's volume more efficiently. The tool takes user parameters, generates the complete blueprint (RTL—Register Transfer Language, the lowest-level chip design), and explores different strategies for routing signals vertically through 3D interconnects and logic blocks. This opens a larger design space to explore without manual tedium.
